text:
Sam: Quick check — I'm about to merge a TF change that adds a Karpenter provisioner override for capacityType=on-demand and sets scaleDownDelaySeconds=300. Wanted to confirm this won't fight with the HPA we have on the inference pods (targetCPU=50%). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4521 :eyes:

Natalie: If scaleDownDelay is longer it just delays node termination, shouldn't affect HPA scaling decisions. The HPA scales based on pod metrics, not node lifecycle. But watch for PodDisruptionBudget interactions — if PDB blocks evictions we'll see nodes not drain and capacity not free up.

Lee: Also watch the provisioner consolidation/TTL. If we keep on-demand fallback, Karpenter might prefer spot first then provision on-demand. Your override forcing on-demand could increase cost for bursty workloads. Are we trying to avoid spot termination for inference latency?

Sam: Yes, this change is to avoid periodic spot terminations that cause tail latency spikes for customer-facing inference. We discussed it in the latency runbook.

Jordan: Two other things — the HPA uses custom metrics from prometheus-adapter (external/prometheus metric: inference_qps). Make sure the adapter's permissions still reference the SA in the same namespace. The PR touched the IRSA role attachment for karpenter, double-check it didn't rename the service account path used by the adapter.

Sam: Good catch. The TF diff shows an IAM role rename: module.eks.module.karpenter.aws_iam_role.karpenter -> aws_iam_role.karpenter_infra. I left a note in the PR asking if this will break the existing annotation on prometheus-adapter SA.

Natalie: If the SA name changes you need to update eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn annotations on those SAs or the adapter will lose permissions and metrics will be missing — HPA will flail to default and maybe scale down incorrectly.

Maria: Also watch Vault secret path for the Karpenter webhook TLS certs. The new TF var moves the secret to secret/data/infra/karpenter/tls in Vault. I already updated the helm values in a separate branch but we need to sync before rollout.

Sam: D'oh — forgot about that vault path. Which helm release did you update?

Maria: infra-monitoring/prometheus-adapter and infra-scheduler/karpenter-webhook. Small change: values.tls.vaultPath = "secret/data/infra/karpenter/tls".

Jordan: Can we run a terraform plan on staging and then a canary deploy? infra-bot: can you queue a plan job for branch sam/provisioner-override?

infra-bot: Plan started for branch sam/provisioner-override on workspace staging. Link: https://ci.redwood/internal/plan/7865 :shipit: 

Lee: Sam, after plan & apply, let's run a quick smoke: 1) confirm prometheus-adapter metrics show up in k8s (kubectl get --raw), 2) create a load generator that bumps inference_qps to trigger HPA scale up, 3) then remove load and measure node scale down timing.

Sam: I'll do that. Any concerns about VPA? We have a VPA object but it's in recommendation mode only for inference-ns. Should we keep it off during rollout?

Natalie: Keep VPA in recommendation mode. If it starts evicting or causing restarts during the node churn it could complicate the test.

Sam: Got it. Final checklist before merge: update SA annotations if IAM role rename, sync Vault path in helm, run staging plan, smoke test for metrics/HPA, confirm PDB is not blocking evictions (pdb minAvailable is 80%). Ping me if you want to join the run.

Jordan: I'll review the PR now. @Natalie please sanity-check the IAM rename impact.

Natalie: Looking. If folks want, I can attach a quick terraform snippet to map the old SA annotation to the new role to avoid downtime: ```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "prom_adapter" {
  metadata {
    name = "prometheus-adapter"
    namespace = "infra-monitoring"
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.karpenter_infra.arn
    }
  }
}
```

Sam: Perfect. I'll wait for infra-bot plan to finish and then merge after we sync Vault changes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
